ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is labeled with input voltage Ui=15V; the upper line first passes through resistor R, then reaches the upper output node on the right side; below is a common loop wire. The two voltage-regulator diodes V1 and V2 are both vertically connected between the upper node after the resistor and the lower common node, so they are shunt voltage-regulating branches connected in parallel across the two ends of output terminal U0. The U0 marked on the right side is the voltage between the upper and lower output terminals. Reasoning: The problem gives the voltage-regulating value of V1 as U_Z1=6V, and the voltage-regulating value of V2 as U_Z2=3V. Since V1 and V2 are connected in parallel at the same output node, when the node voltage rises, V2 with the lower voltage-regulating value will first reach the breakdown voltage-regulating state, clamping the output voltage at about 3V. At this time, the output voltage cannot reach V1's 6V voltage-regulating value, so V1 does not play a 6V clamping role. Therefore the output voltage U0=3V.
